Pianist Frank Strazzeri was born in Rochester, New York on April 24, 1930. He gained valuable experience as a house pianist in a Rochester jazz club and moved to New Orleans in 1954 to work with Al Hirt and Sharkey Bonano. Frank settled in the Los Angeles area in the early 60s and found steady jazz work with Joe Williams, Herb Ellis and Terry Gibbs, and played on many sessions for Pacific Jazz, Verve and Atlantic. He continues to record and perform with the best of the west coast jazz artists.
Frank was interviewed in Los Angeles on February 14, 1999, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.

My name is Monk Rowe and we are filming for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive in Los Angeles. I’m very pleased to have Frank Strazzeri for my guest today, and we’ve had some nice conversations on the phone. We have a few things in common, like where we grew up, Upstate New York — some good musicians came out of there.
